conclusions.rationale: Bounded, testable library rules: trimmed name 1-60, case-insensitive uniqueness, text 1-8000, max 50 prompts, CRUD with delete confirmation and restart persistence. Story 1 scenarios and the has_validation behavioral AC give observable checks.

source_citations.excerpt: A prompt is valid when its trimmed name has 1–60 characters and is unique case-insensitively, and its text has 1–8000 characters. The library holds at most 50 prompts.

conclusions.rationale: Upgrade behavior is explicit and verifiable: existing prompts and selection unchanged, six named starters added once when absent and only under the limit, invalid legacy entries kept and flagged. SC-003 gives the measurable migration check. 'Added once' implies a persisted marker so deleted starters are not re-added; this is a plan concern, not an ambiguity of the requirement.

source_citations.excerpt: the starter prompts Minimal correction, Friendly rephrasing, Clarify, Shorten, Notes and Translate to English are added once when absent by name
Existing prompts that break the new validation rules are kept, flagged invalid and cannot be used until edited.

conclusions.rationale: Trigger-to-prompt mapping (plain=None, post-processing=default, prompt shortcut=its prompt), per-dictation indicator choice that never changes the default, switch-off semantics and a 200 ms non-focus-stealing menu are each observable. The all-platform clause stays testable; per the constitution, Windows/Linux native observation becomes pending release evidence (see info finding).

source_citations.excerpt: The plain dictation shortcut starts with "None", the post-processing shortcut with the default prompt, and a prompt shortcut with its prompt.
The menu opens within 200 ms without taking keyboard focus from the user's application, on every platform where the indicator is shown.

conclusions.rationale: Default vs override resolution, the existing provider set (local custom endpoint, Apple Intelligence where available) and a not-ready state naming the missing item are testable; processing with a not-ready provider skips the AI step and AC-005 lists 'provider not ready' among fallback causes, so the outcome is defined.

source_citations.excerpt: Each prompt uses the default provider and model unless it defines a provider and model override.
A prompt whose provider lacks a required endpoint, model or API key is shown as not ready with the missing item; processing with it skips the AI step.

conclusions.rationale: Failure classes, the 30 s bound over the whole step including retries/fallback, raw-transcript insertion, a 4 s minimum notice, history fields and cancellation are all measurable and backed by SC-001 fault injection. See the non-critical ambiguity on the notice wording ('original was inserted') and on the notice channel when the indicator is hidden.

source_citations.excerpt: or the whole step, including any internal retry or fallback request, exceeds 30 seconds, the initial transcript is inserted, the indicator states for at least 4 seconds that processing failed and the original was inserted
Cancelling during processing inserts nothing; history behaves as today for cancelled dictations.

conclusions.rationale: 0-2 shortcuts per prompt, global activation mode, reuse of 004's shared conflict checker and confirmed removal on delete are testable; Story 5 gives the conflict example.

source_citations.excerpt: A prompt may have 0–2 shortcuts. A prompt shortcut starts a dictation processed with that prompt and follows the global activation mode.

conclusions.rationale: Editable sample prefilled with the last transcript, result with provider/model/duration or error within 30 s, and no insertion nor history write are observable; the async_action behavioral AC defines the panel states.

source_citations.excerpt: A test never inserts text into another application and never writes history.

conclusions.rationale: The CLI operation list, the --clear override reset, delegation of prompt shortcuts to 004 operations, secret exclusion from stdout/stderr/logs, readiness reporting and the JSON-only stdout rule are concrete and consistent with the 008 envelope contract referenced by the spec.

source_citations.excerpt: The settings CLI (008) offers prompt list, create, update, delete, set-default and set-provider-override (provider id and model, or `--clear` to return to the default provider)
Outputs never contain API keys, in stdout, stderr or logs; provider readiness is reported as ready or the missing item.

conclusions.rationale: Maps to AC-001/002/004/006 which define fields, validation, migration and shortcut bounds.

source_citations.excerpt: Persist a validated prompt library with stable ids, names, texts, optional provider/model override and 0–2 shortcuts; migrate existing prompts and add starter prompts once.

conclusions.rationale: Maps to AC-003/006; per-dictation resolution and non-mutation of the default are testable.

source_citations.excerpt: Resolve the prompt of each dictation from its trigger (plain, post-processing or prompt shortcut) and from a per-dictation choice made on the indicator, without changing the default.

conclusions.rationale: Maps to AC-004/005/007; the whole-step 30 s bound including retries is explicit.

source_citations.excerpt: bound the whole step, including internal retries and fallback requests, to 30 seconds.

conclusions.rationale: Maps to AC-005; raw-transcript fallback, failure record and cancellation are specified.

source_citations.excerpt: Insert the initial transcript and record the failure whenever the AI step does not produce a valid result; respect cancellation.

conclusions.rationale: Maps to AC-007; side-effect-free test operation.

source_citations.excerpt: Provide a test operation that never inserts text or writes history.

conclusions.rationale: Maps to AC-008; CLI read/modify operations including override set/clear without secrets.

source_citations.excerpt: Expose prompt read and modify operations, including setting and clearing the per-prompt provider/model override, through the settings CLI without ever outputting API keys.

conclusions.rationale: Measurable: 100% of fault-injected dictations across five named failure classes insert the raw transcript and record the failure.

source_citations.excerpt: In fault-injection tests (provider error, HTTP error, timeout of the whole step, empty result, not ready), 100% of dictations insert the initial transcript and record the failure.

conclusions.rationale: Measurable: zero API key occurrences in a secret scan across all prompt operations.

source_citations.excerpt: Secret scanning of CLI outputs and logs across all prompt operations finds zero API key occurrences.

conclusions.rationale: Measurable by before/after comparison of an upgraded store.

source_citations.excerpt: Upgrading a store with custom prompts keeps all prompts, texts and the selected prompt unchanged.

ambiguities.question: Must the failure notice literally state that the original 'was inserted' even when the insertion method only attempted the paste (no read-back verification)? The program's truthful-outcome principle (006/007) forbids claiming verified insertion; the plan should fix the exact wording (e.g. 'original text sent') and the spec should be aligned through spec-refine if needed.

citations.excerpt: the indicator states for at least 4 seconds that processing failed and the original was inserted

ambiguities.question: When the overlay style is none (indicator hidden), where is the 4-second failure notice shown? The edge case only says prompt choice is limited to shortcuts and settings.

citations.excerpt: The indicator is hidden (overlay style none): prompt choice is available only through shortcuts and settings.

findings.description: AC-005 asks the indicator to state that 'the original was inserted', while the dictation pipeline can only know that an insertion was attempted unless the insertion method verifies it. This wording risks an untruthful message and an unprovable acceptance criterion.
findings.suggestion: Carry to the plan: define the notice wording from the insertion outcome (attempted vs verified) and, if the literal wording must change, update AC-005 through spec-refine rather than leaving acceptance blocked.

citations.excerpt: the indicator states for at least 4 seconds that processing failed and the original was inserted

findings.description: AC-003 requires the 200 ms non-focus-stealing menu on every platform where the indicator is shown; per the constitution only macOS native evidence is required before Implemented, other platforms are pending release evidence.
findings.suggestion: The plan should gate macOS natively and record Windows/Linux as pending release evidence with exact checks, never as blocking implementation steps.

citations.excerpt: on every platform where the indicator is shown.
It never blocks implementation steps, feature completion on the integration branch, or the merge into `dev`; it is never claimed as passed.

findings.description: Quality Engineering (High, Shared, Data then Security) is consistent with QE Analysis (High, every processed dictation and provider credentials, lost/altered text and secret exposure). The Quality Engineering section omits the P1 gates and non-functional expectations, which remain in QE Analysis.
findings.suggestion: No change required; keep both sections aligned when one is edited.

citations.excerpt: primary risk Data (lost or altered text), followed by Security (secret exposure).
**Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** Every processed dictation and provider credentials; **Primary risk:** Lost or altered text and secret exposure
